sources.label: WSJ land-deal report
sources.note: The WSJ URL was reopened but denied the article body. The returned identity and entry claims were independently corroborated by the Los Angeles Times report at https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2009-sep-15-me-wind15-story.html, which identifies the CIM/Renewable Resources Group joint venture as ReNu Resources LLC, the approximately 68,000-acre Onyx Ranch purchase, and the Vernon partial sale. No cutoff-current conclusion relies on WSJ access.

sources.label: CIM SEC filing (2021)
sources.normalizedEvidenceText: As filed with the SEC on January 29, 2021. Jennifer Gandin led or co-led each of the infrastructure acquisitions in CIM Infrastructure Fund I, including Kelso Valley, and continued to hold primary asset management and ongoing oversight responsibilities for Kelso Valley.
sources.note: The direct SEC filing proves CIM Infrastructure Fund I attribution and dated ongoing oversight as of January 29, 2021. It does not prove ownership at the September 2026 cutoff.

sources.label: State Parks acquisition NOD
sources.normalizedEvidenceText: California Department of Parks and Recreation Notice of Determination, State Clearinghouse 2012091066. Eastern Kern County Property Acquisition: acquire up to 59 privately-owned parcels, approximately 28,275 acres, in eastern Kern County from ReNu Resources, LLC. Project approved October 3, 2013.
sources.note: The one-page scanned state Notice of Determination was freshly rendered and visually inspected. It directly names ReNu as seller for up to 59 parcels totaling approximately 28,275 acres and records project approval on October 3, 2013; it does not itself establish closing.

sources.label: Rosedale Onyx Ranch
sources.normalizedEvidenceText: Rosedale-Rio Bravo Water Storage District describes the Onyx Project as the purchase of 3,300 acres commonly referred to as the Onyx Ranch east of Lake Isabella to acquire certain water rights associated with the property.
sources.note: The live water-district page directly verifies Rosedale's 3,300-acre Onyx purchase and water-right purpose. It proves ownership of that component, not complete disposition of every ReNu asset or right.

sources.label: Vernon property record
sources.normalizedEvidenceText: City of Vernon states it purchased 29,722.44 acres in Kern County in 2008, sold 12,420 acres in 2010, retained approximately 16,409.70 acres of vacant undeveloped land, and determined renewable-energy development there was no longer feasible in 2022.
sources.note: The direct City of Vernon record verifies Vernon's purchase, later partial sale, remaining acreage and 2022 infeasibility finding. It does not identify any current ReNu interest.

sources.label: CEQAnet Weldon Solar
sources.normalizedEvidenceText: CEQAnet record 2010031032, received March 8, 2010, is a Notice of Preparation for the Weldon Solar Project by Renewable Resources. It describes a proposed 60-megawatt photovoltaic solar facility on a combined 500 acres.
sources.note: The direct state CEQA record proves only that a 60 MW, 500-acre solar project entered NOP review in March 2010. It does not prove construction, operation, cancellation or transfer.

modelHealthOverrides: The recorder deep URL is session-dependent. The exact instrument row was independently reproduced through a fresh direct date search, but the public index does not expose the deed image, conveyed property, exceptions or reservations.

The WSJ article body returned HTTP 401 during independent reopening. Its identity and entry claims are corroborated by the directly reopened Los Angeles Times report, but no cutoff-current conclusion relies on WSJ access.
The January 2021 SEC disclosure is dated oversight evidence and cannot be converted into September 2026 ownership.
Known transfers to Rosedale, State Parks, Vernon and Trust for Public Land do not reconcile every original acre or rule out retained water, mineral, development or other reserved rights.
The CEQAnet NOP proves a proposed Weldon Solar project in 2010, not construction, operation, cancellation or current ownership.
A negative search for later sales, dissolution or final fund distributions cannot establish continuing ownership or a complete exit.
conclusion: Keep the record deferred without a database or seed mutation. The ReNu/Onyx Ranch identity and several component dispositions are directly supported, and the 2022 ReNu-to-Trust for Public Land quitclaim is independently verified at index level. The deed image and property schedule are unavailable, the current ReNu entity and member state is unverified, and no direct record establishes whether CIM or Renewable Resources Group retains an interest or completed a final exit.
